notes.title: Meeting again
notes.science: Kindness pays when the same pairs meet again and again. A gift today can come back tomorrow.
notes.limits: Kith is small, so everyone meets everyone. A big town does not work this way.
notes.counter: A place that brings creatures together can also keep an old grudge alive.
notes.question: Who did the bench bring together?

sources.label: The Evolution of Cooperation, Axelrod and Hamilton, 1981
Cooperation under the Shadow of the Future, Dal Bó, 2005

notes.title: A place to meet
notes.science: Friends form among people who keep ending up in the same place: the same hall, the same desk row, the same bench.
notes.limits: The bench changes only who meets. It does nothing to how they treat each other.
notes.counter: Some say people make a place warm, and the place only holds what they bring.
notes.question: Would two benches join the village or split it?

sources.label: The Evolution of Trust, Nicky Case

notes.title: Friends of friends
notes.science: Two creatures who share a friend are likely to meet and warm to each other. Ties close into triangles.
notes.limits: Warmth here is one number on each side of a tie.
notes.counter: Real friendship has many kinds of warmth, and a shared friend can also be a rival.
notes.question: What makes a friend thread snap?

sources.label: Empirical Analysis of an Evolving Social Network, Kossinets and Watts, 2006
The Strength of Weak Ties, Granovetter, 1973

pim: The bench is warm in the mornings. I sit there and wait for whoever comes, and somebody always comes.
